en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Ovādavagga 29.
The Training Rule on Those Who Have Been Fully Matured.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was a regular visitor to a certain family, having been provided with a constant supply of food by them.
On one occasion, the elder bhikkhus had been invited by that householder.
Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā dressed herself, took her bowl and robe, and went to that family. Having arrived, she said this to the householder:
“Householder, why is so much solid food and soft food prepared?
“I have invited the elders, noble lady.
“But who are those elders, householder?”

“Venerable Sāriputta, Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, Venerable Mahākaccāna, Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika, Venerable Mahākappina, Venerable Mahācunda, Venerable Anuruddha, Venerable Revata, Venerable Upāli, Venerable Ānanda, and Venerable Rāhula.
“But householder, while these great nāgas are present, whom do you invite as servants?
“But who, Venerable lady, are those great nāgas?”
“Venerable Devadatta, venerable Kokālika, venerable Kaṭamodakatissaka, venerable Khaṇḍadeviyā-putta, venerable Samuddadatta.
This was the interrupted conversation of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā when those elder bhikkhus entered.
“Is it true, householder, that you have invited the Great Nāgas?”
“Just now, noble lady, you made her a slave-girl; now you have made her a great nāga!
He then had her cast out from the house and cut off her regular supply of food.
Those monks who were of few desires... [as above] ...were indignant, disparaged [him], and complained, saying:
“How indeed can Devadatta knowingly eat almsfood prepared by a nun?
… [as before] … “Is it true, Devadatta, that you knowingly eat almsfood prepared by a nun?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“… How can you, foolish man, knowingly eat almsfood prepared by a bhikkhunī?
This, foolish man, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:
“Whosoever, a monk, knowingly eats almsfood that has been prepared by a nun, there is an offense of expiation.
In this way, this training rule was laid down for the monks by the Blessed One.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu who had gone forth from Rājagaha went to his family home.
The people, saying, “It has been a long time since the venerable one arrived,” prepared a meal with great care for him.
A bhikkhunī who was a frequent visitor to that family said this to those people:
“Friend, this is the meal for the deceased.
Then that bhikkhu,
being apprehensive because he knew, “The Blessed One has prohibited eating almsfood prepared by a bhikkhunī,” did not accept it.
He was unable to go for alms and his meal was cut off.
Then that bhikkhu went to the monastery and reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma on this occasion and in this context, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, bhikkhus, to eat almsfood that was prepared by a bhikkhunī, knowing it to have been previously undertaken for a householder.
And thus, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:”

“Whosoever, however, a bhikkhu, knowing that almsfood has been prepared by a bhikkhunī, should eat it, except in the case of what was previously undertaken by a householder, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Whosoever, however, means whoever of such a kind... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Knows" means:
She either knows it herself, or others inform her of it, or she informs him herself.
"Bhikkhunī" means one who has received full ordination in both Saṅghas.
“Bringing to maturity” means:

toward those who previously were unwilling to give or unwilling to act, one says, “The venerable one is a reciter; the venerable one is learned; the venerable one is a master of the Suttas; the venerable one is an upholder of the Vinaya; the venerable one is a preacher of the Dhamma; give to the venerable one; do for the venerable one. This is what is called “bringing to maturity. Almsfood is as follows:
One of the five kinds of cooked food.
"Except for what was previously prepared by a householder" means excluding that which was prepared by a householder.
“Householder’s initiative” means that it is either from relatives, or from those who have invited him,
or something already prepared for ordinary use. If he accepts it, thinking, “I will eat it, except as a householder’s initiative,” there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For every mouthful, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
If he eats what has been prepared, perceiving it as such—except for food previously offered by a householder—there is an offense of expiation.
If he eats what has been prepared while being in doubt about it—except for food previously offered by a householder—there is an offense of wrongdoing (*dukkaṭa*).

If one eats what has been prepared by someone who has not yet reached the age of twenty, perceiving it as unprepared—except in the case of what was previously prepared for a householder—there is no offense.

If one eats what has been prepared by someone who is fully ordained on only one side (a male novice), perceiving it as prepared—except in the case of what was previously prepared for a householder—there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one eats what has been prepared by someone who has not yet reached the age of twenty, perceiving it as prepared, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If [the person] is not yet matured and one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If [the person] is not yet matured and one perceives them as not yet matured, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
Previously, during her time as a householder,
she brought the female trainee (sikkhamānā) to maturity and brought the female novice (sāmaṇerī) to maturity.
Except for the five kinds of food, there is no offense in all other cases;
nor is there an offense for one who is insane or for a first-time offender.
The ninth training rule concerning those who have been brought to maturity is finished.
